articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Winter Cleanup Across Foundry Row
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in January.
body: Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings. The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

Cyrus Nakamura, who has lived in Foundry Row for 20 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The plan calls for Saturday cleanup day along Laurel Drive, with work expected to start in January.
Public works estimates the work will take about 20 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Sergio Renner, 80, Playground Monitor
articles.deck: Friends remember Sergio Renner for the many years of service to Upper Commons.
body: Sergio Renner died in June at home on Linden Court, at the age of 80. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Upper Commons.

Born in Upper Commons in the years after the war, Sergio Renner spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Upper Commons Historical Society in his or her name.

articles.title: Then & Now: St. Brendan’s Hall, 1983 and 2019
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal. A 1983 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Linden Place from the corner of Briar Avenue.
Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
